correctness.rationale: Radial integration gives μ_j=β B(j+1,β), with μ_0=1. On the unnormalized mode r^|j| e^(ijθ), projection after z^a multiplication yields the one coefficient μ_[(a+|j|+|j+a|)/2]/μ_|j+a|. Composing and normalizing gives all three coefficient branches including k=n,m. Both ordered products telescope on each tail (j≥0 and j≤−(2n+d)); reflection k→2n+d−k negates the normalized coefficient and forces the midpoint to vanish if integral. Distinct output modes give exactly the singular-value list. An independent Python Fraction diagnostic constructed the moments with μ_j/μ_(j−1)=j/(j+β), worked on unnormalized Fourier modes, and compared the two products with the three branches after removing the common normalization sqrt(μ_(2n+d−k)/μ_k). It agreed exactly on all 6048 checks for β=1/5,1/2,4/5, n=1..12, d=1..7 and −3≤k≤2n+d+3, including antisymmetry after clearing the square roots. The frozen checker was read, not run. For the infinite limit a useful independent reconstruction avoids differentiation: with F_l(k)=μ_l/μ_(l−k), the exact quotient F_(l+1)/F_l is 1+βk/[(l+1+β)(l−k+1)] for l≥k. Summing these d increments at l=n..n+d−1 and multiplying by the moment square-root prefactor gives the left branch with a minus sign. Gamma ratios show F_l≤C((l−k+1)/(l+1))^β and the square root is bounded there. Thus k=n−u gives the uniform bound C n^(−β)(1+u)^(β−1); reflection and the finitely many intermediate modes give the global bound. For t=k/n in a compact subset of (0,1), the same increments give nc/d→−β t(1−t)^(β−1)(t/(2−t))^(β/2). To justify the bulk Riemann sum rigorously, trim both ends of the left interval: the interface near t=1 costs O(ε^(1−p(1−β))) in rescaled mass, and near t=0 the uniform bound gives |c|≤C/n and hence O(ε). This supplies the endpoint detail implicit in Step 3. For fixed signed r=k−n, the three branches give n^βc→Gβ(|r|)−Gβ(|d−r|). The differences Gβ(j+1)−Gβ(j)=βGβ(j)/(j+1) are positive and decreasing and ∼βj^(β−1), so the tail gives exactly the stated convergence threshold and the maximum occurs at r=0,d. The same majorant yields dominated convergence of the upper-regime mass and tightness of the scaled maximum. In the critical region R≤u≤εn the exact increments have F_l=(u/n)^β[1+O(1/u+u/n)], the prefactor is 1+O((u+1)/n), and βk/[(l+1+β)(l−k+1)]=(β/u)[1+O(1/u+u/n)]. This proves the required uniform intermediate law. Reflection shifts u by the fixed d only; each tail contributes the same harmonic log coefficient. At fixed R,ε the central and outer strips have O(1) mass after n^(βp) scaling, so the two-sided coefficient is 2(βd)^p. All results require fixed d,β,p and measure asymptotic mass, not membership of individual finite-rank operators.
